title: Emrys and the Portrait
premise: Retired detective Noor Fairweather, now barely keeping her bookshop afloat, is hired by a nervous stranger to prove that a murder has not yet happened — the predicted killing of art restorer Emrys Vale, whose forged portrait of a dead heiress sits at the center of an inheritance fraud. As Noor investigates, she discovers Emrys is alive but in hiding, and that three earlier 'accidents' were silencing witnesses to the forgery. The client, it turns out, is Emrys himself, testing whether Noor can be trusted before he surfaces as the witness who could convict a powerful family. In the end, Noor exposes the conspiracy through the painting itself, chooses justice over legal safety by leaking the evidence, and gives Emrys a new identity — while her bookshop, ironically, finally thrives on the notoriety.
about_author: Ada Sterling is the pen name of a former forensic archivist who spent fifteen years cataloguing cold-case evidence before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage on the Cornish coast, where the fog does half her plotting for her.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid Too Much
chapters.summary: Noor Fairweather, closing up her failing bookshop, is approached by a pale, sweating man who pays triple in advance to prove a murder hasn't happened yet — the future death of one Emrys Vale. His urgency unsettles her; his cash saves her. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: wary curiosity masking financial desperation.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, One Pattern
chapters.summary: Noor reviews her private files: three deaths the police ruled accidental — a fall, a fire, a drowning — all connected to the Vale estate's contested will. She never published her findings; now the pattern points somewhere new. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: the old detective instinct reawakening like a scar itching before rain.

chapters.title: The Portrait of a Dead Woman
chapters.summary: Noor visits the Ashcombe gallery and studies the portrait of heiress Lavinia Vale, allegedly painted decades ago. The varnish is wrong; the grief in the eyes is too modern. The restorer credited: Emrys Vale. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: aesthetic unease hardening into professional certainty.

chapters.title: A Family That Owns the Town
chapters.summary: Noor probes the Vale family: patriarch Aldous Vale, heir Marcus, and lawyer Corinne Blake, who controls the estate paperwork. Everyone speaks of Emrys in past tense — 'poor Emrys, such a tragedy.' POV: Noor. Emotional beat: the chill of a town that has agreed, collectively, not to look.

chapters.title: Dead Men Don't Buy Paint Thinners
chapters.summary: Following receipts, Noor finds Emrys Vale purchased supplies at a hardware shop eleven days ago — after his supposed death. The shopkeeper swears it was someone else. Someone is lying, and it isn't the ledger. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into fear — if Emrys lives, so does the murder.

chapters.title: The Man Behind the Curtain Wall
chapters.summary: Noor tracks the purchases to a derelict chapel outside town and finds Emrys Vale alive, gaunt, and terrified, living behind a false wall. He denies hiring her. She realizes her client was someone else entirely. POV: alternating Noor/Emrys. Emotional beat: two hunters discovering they're both prey.

chapters.title: What the Forger Knows
chapters.summary: Emrys confesses: he painted the fake Lavinia portrait under coercion years ago, and the three 'accidents' were witnesses who wavered. He is the last living witness — and the next body. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: guilt finally spoken aloud, lighter and heavier at once.

chapters.title: Who Hired the Detective?
chapters.summary: Noor traces her anonymous client through the payment trail to a shell company — and then to Corinne Blake, the family lawyer. Why would the conspirator hire the one detective who might catch them? POV: Noor. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing she was hired as cover, not as protection.

chapters.title: Insurance Against Conviction
chapters.summary: Noor confronts Corinne, who coolly admits hiring her: if Noor publicly proves Emrys is alive, the family can brand him a fraudster and destroy his credibility before any trial. Noor was meant to be their weapon. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: fury and grudging respect for a flawless trap.

chapters.title: The Bookshop Watcher
chapters.summary: Marcus Vale begins visiting the bookshop, buying books he never reads, watching Noor. A brick through her window that night carries no message except the message itself. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: fear moving from abstract to personal; her sanctuary breached.

chapters.title: Emrys Runs
chapters.summary: Spooked by Noor's confrontation with Corinne, Emrys flees the chapel, convinced Noor sold him out. He vanishes into the city with the one thing that matters: photographs of his original sketches proving the forgery. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: paranoia devouring the only alliance he had.

chapters.title: The Drowned Archivist
chapters.summary: A fourth death: the county records clerk who authenticated the portrait's provenance is found drowned. Police call it accidental. Noor knows better — and knows she's running out of witnesses, and time. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: grief and rage fusing into resolve.

chapters.title: Reading the Police File
chapters.summary: Noor calls in an old favor from a sympathetic constable and reads the official files on all four deaths. Each investigation was quietly closed within days. Someone above the police is protecting the Vales. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: disillusionment — the law itself is part of the conspiracy.

chapters.title: Finding the Ghost
chapters.summary: Using Emrys's known habits — cheap cafés, secondhand art books — Noor tracks him to a flophouse. Their reunion is hostile until she shows him the drowned archivist's file. He understands: running won't save him either. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: broken trust slowly re-knitting into partnership.

chapters.title: The Plan Neither of Them Likes
chapters.summary: Noor proposes a dangerous gambit: authenticate the forgery publicly, force the family to act, and catch them in the attempt. Emrys must pose as a dead man walking — bait. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: the moral weight of risking a life to save a principle.

chapters.title: Opening Night
chapters.summary: At a gala unveiling the portrait's 'restoration,' Emrys appears unannounced among the guests, alive and recognizable. The room freezes. Aldous Vale smiles like a man watching a trap close on someone else. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into defiance.

chapters.title: The Attempt
chapters.summary: That night, two men come for Emrys at his safehouse. Noor, waiting, records everything — but the attackers are professionals, and the plan nearly kills them both. They escape with the recording and a torn piece of one attacker's jacket. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: adrenaline, then the cold aftermath of how close it was.

chapters.title: The Jacket and the Money
chapters.summary: The jacket traces to a security firm owned by Marcus Vale; the payment trail leads back to Corinne Blake. Noor has the chain: forgery, four murders, ordered from the top. But every court in reach belongs to the Vales. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: victory shadowed by the question — justice through whom?

chapters.title: Corinne's Choice
chapters.summary: Noor corners Corinne privately, offering her testimony against the family in exchange for immunity from exposure. Corinne, realizing Aldous will make her the fifth accident, hesitates — then hands over the estate's hidden ledgers. POV: Corinne. Emotional beat: self-preservation dressed up as conscience.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Knowing the courts are bought, Noor releases everything — ledgers, recording, Emrys's sketches — to national press simultaneously, making suppression impossible. Arrests follow within days; Aldous Vale falls publicly and irreversibly. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: the cost and clarity of choosing truth over procedure.

chapters.title: A New Name for Emrys
chapters.summary: With the case closed, Noor helps Emrys disappear properly this time — by choice. New papers, a coastal town, a small legitimate studio restoring honest paintings. He leaves her one gift: a true portrait, painted from memory, of the woman Lavinia really was. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: release; identity finally chosen rather than imposed.

chapters.title: The Portrait in the Window
chapters.summary: Months later, the bookshop thrives on its famous case. In the front window hangs the true portrait of Lavinia, unlabeled. A customer asks about it; Noor says only, 'It's a story about what people survive.' POV: Noor. Emotional beat: quiet peace — power corrupted, justice served, identities remade.
